title: The substance of things hoped for (Hebrews 11)
hookLine: Abel, Noah, Abraham, Sara and the long list of the faithful

cards: Names written inside the cover of an old Bible. Photos stuck to a fridge. A grandmother who prayed through a war.

An uncle who started over in a new country with one suitcase. Many families keep a list like this somewhere. Nobody on it is perfect, and all of them kept walking toward something they couldn't see yet.

Hebrews eleven is that list for the whole Church. After ten chapters on Christ the high priest, and before the hard advice of chapter twelve, the writer stops and reads out the family names. He opens with a definition.

teach.b: The Douay-Rheims gives it like this: "Now faith is the substance of things to be hoped for, the evidence of things that appear not." Substance first.
The Greek word is hypostasis, literally what stands underneath: a foundation, the thing that holds something up. In this line faith isn't a mood or a guess.
It's the ground under a hope, giving it somewhere to stand before it arrives. Then evidence: a conviction about what can't be seen yet. Then the names, each opening the same way: by faith.

teach.h: BY FAITH: ABEL, NOAH, ABRAHAM, SARA.
teach.b: By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice than Cain. Noah built an ark for a flood nobody had ever seen. Abraham "went out, not knowing whither he went."
Sara, long past the age for children, received strength to conceive, because she believed that the one who promised was faithful.
Then Moses, Rahab, and a rush of names the writer says there isn't time to finish: Gideon, Samson, David, Samuel, the prophets. Here's the surprise.
The chapter says plainly that these people died without receiving what was promised. They saw it from far off and greeted it, like travelers waving at a city on the horizon.
And the last verse says they would not be made perfect without us.

teach.h: FAITH IS THE SUBSTANCE OF THINGS TO BE HOPED FOR.
teach.b: The list isn't closed; it's waiting for more names. Catholics hear the communion of saints in this: the faithful who have gone before are still one family with the living.
The next chapter calls them a cloud of witnesses, surrounding the race.

how: Catholics hear parts of Hebrews 11 in the Sunday and weekday readings at Mass, and the chapter's list of the faithful is often read alongside the Church's teaching on the communion of saints.

o: believing something with no reason at all
a strong feeling that things will turn out well
the ground a hope stands on before it arrives

games.q: the list of the faithful — tap the pairs.
p: an ark for a flood never seen
believed the one who promised was faithful

s: Hebrews 11 says the faithful all lived to see the promise come true
the chapter says they died without receiving it, greeting it from far off.
the Greek word behind substance means what stands underneath
hypostasis: a foundation, the thing that holds something up.
Hebrews says the faithful of old would not be made perfect without us
the chapter ends that way: the list is still open.

games.q: you're Noah. you've been warned of a flood nobody has ever seen, and the ground is dry. what do you do?
o: build the ark now, on dry ground.
wait until the first rain to be sure.
warn the neighbors and stay put.
games.why: by faith Noah built the ark for things not yet seen. that's the whole chapter in one picture: acting on a hope before it arrives.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose faith held you up, alive or gone: a grandparent, a teacher, a friend who kept going through something hard.
Say their name quietly, then finish the line the way Hebrews does, by faith, they..., and let it end however it ends: kept a promise, got up early to pray, forgave.
If you pray, thank God for them by name; if not, hold the name with gratitude.

wordCard.voice: Faith. In Hebrews eleven, the substance of things hoped for: the ground a hope stands on before it arrives. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: faith, trust. Hebrews 11 opens with it and repeats it name after name.
